**Mesh Mix-S2C 2.0.0, test build 2.** This is a test build for trying the new engine before 2.0.0 comes out. It is a pre-release: the apps won't offer it as an update, and people on 1.6.0 stay on 1.6.0 until 2.0.0 is out. If you're testing, thank you!

Mesh Mix-S2C is Manifold Mesh Mix merged with [stl2curves](https://github.com/Duvdivan/stl2curves) by Duvdivan. It's the same app with a new engine that combines the two converters.

## What's new

- **A merged engine for STL and 3MF files.** stl2curves' feature finder (screw threads, fillets, holes and radii at their designed sizes, freeform patches) now feeds Manifold Mesh Mix's builder, which checks every face against the mesh. Auto and CAD use it for STL files and for 3MF projects converted as one STEP, laid out as on the plate. A 3MF split into parts (the "Split 3MF projects into parts" setting, on by default), OBJ and PLY files, and Smooth still use 1.6.0's engine for now.
- **New since test build 1:**
  - 3MF projects go through the merged engine (a 38-part P1S riser plate went from far off to good; a threaded nut from 3,272 freeform faces to 297 true faces).
  - A part whose curved faces fitted well but had two tiny broken flat faces is now saved with CAD faces instead of flat triangles.
  - Very fine meshes are welded more carefully, and a last face repair can no longer turn a neighbouring face inside out.
- **Measured on 150 test parts** (CAD exports, printed parts, scans and coarse meshes up to 300,000 triangles): 143 come out good by our benchmark's judge. Good means a valid closed solid, its volume within 1% of the mesh's, and 99% of the surface within 0.1 mm both ways.
- **Bodies pulled straight along one direction** (tubes, extrusions) are recognised as such, so Auto picks CAD faces for them instead of smooth surfaces.
- **Screw threads with rounded crests** (pipe threads, for example) are found, as long as they wind at least 3 turns.
- **Small self-crossing spots in a mesh are mended more carefully**, so they no longer leave a dent or a bump in the result.
- **"Flat faces" is shown plainly.** When neither CAD faces nor smooth surfaces follow a mesh closely enough, Auto keeps the mesh's own triangles as a valid solid. The app now says so instead of looking like a hidden preset.
- **The new name and logo.** Your settings carry over.

## What to try

- Mechanical parts with threads, holes, fillets and chamfers: compare the face count and the shape in your CAD program with 1.6.0.
- Files that went wrong in 1.6.0.
- Big meshes (over 300,000 triangles): note how long they take.

## Known problems

These test parts don't come out good yet, and we're working on them:

- Parts where repair leaves pieces overlapping or touching themselves can come out with errors (in our set: a repeater mount and a P1S riser body).
- A few parts come out valid but slightly off the mesh, by 0.2 to 2 mm in places (in our set: a chute, a toolbox and a solar arm mount, whose mesh has a crumpled patch).
- Very fine meshes of small parts (hundreds of thousands of triangles on a part a few centimetres across) can take an hour or more and come out with errors.
- Big meshes (over 300,000 triangles) are slow; huge ones (millions of triangles) may take hours.
- OBJ and PLY files, split 3MF projects and Smooth still use 1.6.0's engine (see above).

## Downloads

- **macOS 14+ (Apple silicon):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-test.2-macOS-arm64.zip`. Unzip it and drag the app into Applications. The first time, right-click it and choose **Open** (the app isn't notarized). It installs next to 1.6.0 ("Manifold Mesh Mix"), so you can keep both while testing.
- **Windows 10/11 (64-bit):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-test.2-Windows-x64-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns, click **More info → Run anyway**. It replaces 1.6.0 if that's installed.
- **Linux (x86-64):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-test.2-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and double-click it.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.

When 2.0.0 comes out, a test build offers it as an update like any other version. To go back to 1.6.0 before then, install it from the [1.6.0 release](https://github.com/STL2CURVES-MMM/Mesh-Mix-S2C/releases/tag/v1.6.0).

## Reporting a problem

Select the file in the queue and use **Save Report…**, then attach the report to a new issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/STL2CURVES-MMM/Mesh-Mix-S2C/issues). The report has your settings and the engine's log. Attach the mesh too if you can share it.
